SUBJECT: Conditional Use Permit (CUP 24-07)

PROJECT PROPOSAL/REQUEST: A request for approval of a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to allow
the sales of alcohol (ABC License Type 41 - beer and wine) for on-site consumption in conjunction with
an existing restaurant (“Guajillo”) located at 8534 Long Beach Boulevard, Unit D. The project does not
include site or tenant improvements.

Project Overview

•  General Plan Designation: Commercial

•  Zoning: Urban Neighborhood (UN)

•  Project Location: 8534 Long Beach Blvd., Unit D

•  Assessor’s Parcel Numbers: 6211-026-032 & 6211-026-033

•  Applicant: Victor A. Reyes Rosas, “Guajillo” Restaurant

BACKGROUND:

•  Site Characteristics: The subject site is an existing dine-in Mexican food restaurant (Guajillo) located
  within a multi-tenant shopping center with surface-level parking on two parcels measuring
  approximately 68,083 square feet. The site is bounded by Long Beach Boulevard to the west,
  Independence Avenue to the south, and a mix of residential properties to the east and north. The
  shopping center comprises a seven-tenant primary building spanning along the easterly and northerly
  edges of the site, a two-tenant building pad at the southwest corner of the site, and surface-level parking
  throughout the remainder of the site. The subject site is occupied by a mix of retail stores, laundromat,
  nail shop, dentistry office, donut shop, and a couple restaurants, including Guajillo.

  Guajillo is located in the southerly tenant space of the primary building, occupying approximately 1,406
  square feet. The restaurant consists of a dining area adjoining the main entrance, a point-of-sale counter
  and refrigerator which divide the dining area from the kitchen and storage areas located at the rear of
  the tenant space, and restrooms that also adjoin the dining area.

•  Surroundings: Surrounding properties include automotive repair facilities across Long Beach
  Boulevard to the west; a Southern Pacific railroad adjoining Independence Avenue to the south; and a
  church and a mix of single-family and multi-family residential properties to the north and east.

ANALYSIS:

•  Municipal Code Requirements for a CUP: Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section
  11.21.030, Table 11.21-3 (Allowed Land Uses, Urban Mixed-Use Zones), the sales of alcoholic
  beverages for on-site consumption in conjunction with a restaurant may be permitted provided a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is granted by the Planning Commission.

•  Required findings for a CUP: Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be granted, the
  Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following findings, as
  applicable to the property:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of
  this title or the city’s General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the
  existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood.

•  Municipal Code Conditions of Approval for Alcoholic Beverage Sales: Pursuant to SGMC Section
  11.42.070, any CUP for alcoholic beverage sales shall include minimum mandatory conditions which
  are included in the proposed resolution.

Business Operations

Guajillo has been operating at this location since June 2022. The business is currently operated seven days
a week from 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. The applicant is seeking a new Department of Alcoholic Beverage
Control (ABC) License Type 41 to be able to offer beer and wine to customers as part of their dining
experience. Allowing alcohol service can enhance the overall atmosphere and appeal of the restaurant. The
restaurant would like to provide a more complete and enjoyable experience for guests, appealing to
customers who prefer to have the option to drink while dining out. It also aims to attract a broader customer
base, including those who enjoy pairing wine or beer with their meals. Furthermore, alcohol sales will
potentially increase revenue for the business.

The applicant proposes to store bottled alcohol within the refrigerator located next to the point-of-sale
counter. The alcoholic beverages are proposed to be served at the cashier counter, when a customer is
paying for a meal. A standard condition is included that alcohol may only be consumed within the enclosed
building on premises, except for permitted outdoor seating areas for on-sale use. Alcohol is proposed to be
served between 8:00am and 9:00pm, aligning with the business hours of operation.

Security measures are not proposed; however, a recommended condition of approval will require the
applicant to install a video surveillance system to monitor the premises on a 24-hour basis. With the
recommended condition, including other standard conditions of approval, it is anticipated that the proposed
sales of beer and wine will not cause nuisances or compromise the public health, safety, and welfare.

Off-Street Parking

Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.33.030, the minimum requirement for a dine-in restaurant measuring less
than 4,000 square feet in floor area is 1 parking space per 100 square feet of gross floor area. A total of 14
parking spaces are required specifically for the subject restaurant. The subject site is developed with a total
of 89 surface-level parking spaces. Therefore, 75 parking spaces are dedicated to the other uses within the
property.

Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.33.030(D), Existing Facilities, a modification to a building or use shall be
subject to conformance with the parking standards based on the following:

  1.  One enlargement or expansion limited to one percent of the total building area may be permitted
  without increasing parking to the standards.

  2.  All additional enlargement or expansion shall be contingent upon concurrent provision of the
  required number of parking spaces or parking area as designated by this chapter (Ch. 11.33).

This project only involves a request for an ABC license. Therefore, the project will not be subject to
compliance with the current off-street parking requirements since the business will simply augment its
alcohol inventory for customers and will not physically be expanded into adjacent tenant spaces; and the
building will not be enlarged, altered, or modified.

CUP Analysis

In granting approval of a CUP, the Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the
following findings, as applicable to the property, as found in SGMC Section 11.52.030. Justification for
each finding is included in the proposed resolution.

A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of this title
  or the City’s General Plan.

B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the existing
  and future land uses of the applicable zone.

C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character
  or function of the neighborhood.

Conclusion

Based on the above analysis, the staff has determined that with the recommended conditions of approval,
the proposed project will comply with the SGMC, and all the required findings in support of a CUP will be
made.

categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities”, in that the
project will not result in any alterations or expansion to the existing buildings within the project site.
Further, no exceptions to the exemption apply; there is no reasonable possibility that the activity will have
a significant effect on the environment due to unusual circumstances. The property is already developed,
